title: Aurora Health - POC timeline & milestones
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC focused on inference latency and cost for Aurora Health's clinical summarization workload. Success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for short summaries, throughput 50 req/s with batching, no PHI leaving VPC. Milestones: kickoff, infra/access setup, mid-point benchmark review, exec readout. Next steps include sharing security docs, test dataset, and scheduling access window.
topics: Workload sizing and expected token lengths
next_steps: Maya to share POC statement of work and pricing sheet (due 2026-09-16)
Jordan to request temporary test account and docs for VPC peering (due 2026-09-18)
Aurora to send redacted sample dataset and success criteria rubric (Sarah/Tom) (due 2026-09-17)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Set up a sandbox dedicated environment and send access details (due 2026-09-21)
Leah Ortiz: Confirm encryption/KMS requirements and list of compliance docs needed (due 2026-09-20)
Maya Patel: Share SOC2 + ISO attestation and network diagram, include Redwood Private options (due 2026-09-16)
Dr. Sarah Kim: Provide 200 redacted clinical notes for benchmarking (due 2026-09-17)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, and Jordan is here from our solutions engineering team. Can everyone say hi quick?
00:08 Dr. Sarah Kim: Hi, Sarah here, hi Maya, thanks.
00:11 Raj Patel: Raj from platform.
00:13 Leah Ortiz: Leah, CISO.
00:15 Tom Alvarez: Tom, product.
00:18 Maya Patel: Great. The goal today is to scope a POC for the clinical summarization pipeline you described over email — focus on latency, throughput, and data controls. We'll run through success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and a proposed timeline with milestones. Sound good?
00:29 Dr. Sarah Kim: Yeah that's right, we mainly want to validate that the model can summarize notes quickly and keep everything inside our VPC, and also show unit cost numbers so we can budget.
00:38 Jordan Lee: Quick intro from me, I'm Jordan, I'll own the infra and benchmarking side for Redwood. We'll propose a dedicated sandbox for you, or if you prefer we can do a private deployment behind your VPC.
00:49 Raj Patel: Probably start with a dedicated sandbox, we'd like to avoid full private for the POC unless the perf looks off. Also we need to know how you handle PHI, retention.
00:58 Leah Ortiz: For compliance: SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS integration — we need to evaluate. We'll want to see encryption at rest, key control, and an SLA for retention.
01:10 Maya Patel: Totally. We'll share our SOC2 + ISO docs and a network diagram. For KMS we support customer-managed keys, integration notes in the security pack.
01:20 Tom Alvarez: On success criteria, operationally leadership wants p95 latency under 200ms for short summaries and good throughput for batch processing. We also need summaries to pass a quality rubric we can share.
01:32 Jordan Lee: Helpful — when you say short summaries, what's the token distribution? average input length?
01:37 Dr. Sarah Kim: Most notes are 150–600 tokens, median around 320 tokens. Output summaries are 30–80 tokens typically.
01:45 Jordan Lee: Got it. For that profile we expect per-token latencies to be reasonable; with Redwood Dedicated we can aim for p95 <200ms for single-turn generation if we tune batch size and use KV cache for repeated prefixes. Small caveat, if you have very high concurrency simultaneous requests, we may need larger pool or autoscaling.
02:07 Raj Patel: What's your baseline cost estimate? We need to compare to our in-house infra run.
02:12 Maya Patel: We'll give a cost estimate in the SOW — it factors in GPU-hours, batching efficiency, and prefix caching. For the POC, we'll provide a cost projection and also a benchmark run so you can see real tokens/s.
02:24 Leah Ortiz: Regarding data residency — all PHI must remain in our VPC or on-prem. Can the POC be done with Redwood Private?
02:32 Jordan Lee: Yes, we support Private deployments. For speed of onboarding, we typically do a sandbox dedicated run that peers to your VPC via AWS VPC peering or a private network path; alternatively an on-prem package is possible but adds time.
02:46 Dr. Sarah Kim: Timeline wise what's realistic? We have an executive readout end of October.
02:50 Maya Patel: If we start now, here's a proposed 6-week timeline: Week 0 - kickoff and access setup; Week 1-2 - baseline benchmarks and tuning; Week 3 - mid-point benchmark review and quality checks; Week 4-5 - final tuning and scale tests; Week 6 - exec readout and handoff. That lines up with late Oct for an exec presentation.
03:12 Tom Alvarez: That works. Can you outline concrete milestones and owners?
03:16 Maya Patel: Sure — Kickoff (this week): confirm test dataset and security checklist. Access/setup (by 2026-09-21): Jordan sets up sandbox and peering. Mid-point review (week of 2026-10-05): share preliminary benchmark results and quality regression checks. Final exec readout (week of 2026-10-19): present final numbers and recommendations.
03:33 Raj Patel: For benchmarks, we need p95 latency, p50, throughput at target concurrency, and cost per 1K tokens. Also examples where quality regressed vs current model.
03:43 Jordan Lee: We'll run a set: 1) single-request latency distribution for sample set, 2) throughput with simulated concurrency at 10/25/50 reqs/s, 3) A/B comparisons for quality on your rubric, 4) KV cache/continuous batching effects. We'll deliver raw logs and a spreadsheet.
03:59 Leah Ortiz: Can you guarantee that logs won't contain PHI?
04:02 Jordan Lee: We'll mask or strip PHI in any logs we share. For internal benchmarking we can run inside your VPC so logs never leave.
04:10 Dr. Sarah Kim: On quality, our rubric includes clinical fidelity, hallucination rate under 2%, and usefulness score above 4/5. We'll provide the rubric and annotated examples.
04:21 Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll incorporate the rubric into the eval harness. For success criteria we'll codify: p95 latency <200ms for median input, throughput 50 req/s sustained with target latency under 300ms, hallucination rate <2% on your rubric, all data kept in VPC and keys under your KMS.
04:40 Tom Alvarez: If you hit that, leadership is likely to greenlight Dedicated or Private.
04:45 Raj Patel: Any known gotchas on model variants or quantization? We run a bunch of clinical-specific tokens and want to ensure no tokenization edge cases.
04:53 Jordan Lee: Good point — model selection matters. We'll recommend a quantized 16-bit or 8-bit variant depending on memory and latency tradeoffs. Tokenization edge cases we can test with your corpus; we sometimes see small differences with custom medical tokens, we can add those to the tokenizer.
05:07 Maya Patel: For the POC we suggest three benchmark profiles: small-latency optimized model, mid cost/quality balanced model, and a high-quality model. That way we show the trade space.
05:18 Dr. Sarah Kim: Can you run on our pre-production VPC? We need to ensure keys never leave.
05:22 Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll request a peering and an IAM role for access. We'll provide steps for creating a role and the minimal policy.
05:30 Leah Ortiz: We'll need to review the network diagram and firewall rules, and an action item for us to open ports for the peering.
05:36 Maya Patel: Noted. We'll send the network diagram and minimal ports required.
05:40 Tom Alvarez: Benchmarks: what's the typical duration to get reliable numbers?
05:44 Jordan Lee: For an initial baseline, 24–48 hours of scheduled load is enough to understand p95 and throughput behavior. For stability and autoscaling behaviors we'll run a 72-hour soak. For the POC we'll plan a quick 48-hour run during week 2 and a longer 72-hour run in week 4.
06:00 Raj Patel: What about cost for that benchmarking? We need to budget for GPU hours.
06:04 Maya Patel: We'll put estimated GPU-hour costs in the SOW and offer a POC discount for the first month. The SOW will include estimated token cost, GPU hours, and breakouts by profile.
06:15 Dr. Sarah Kim: On success criteria — one more ask: we want a regression alert if any metric deviates by more than 10% from baseline. Can Redwood integrate with our Datadog alerts?
06:26 Jordan Lee: Yes, we can push metrics to Datadog or provide a webhook. We'll include a tracing hook and per-route latency breakdown.
06:34 Leah Ortiz: Okay, security doc list? We need SOC2, penetration test summary, data flow diagram, encryption specifics, and RBAC details.
06:43 Maya Patel: We'll attach our security pack and the private deployment checklist. Also will note differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private in the doc.
06:51 Tom Alvarez: A practical question: who does the exec readout? Is it Redwood or Aurora presenting together?
06:55 Maya Patel: Typically we co-present — you lead on clinical outcomes, we present the performance and operational recommendations. We can prepare a slide deck and a short appendix with raw numbers.
07:06 Dr. Sarah Kim: Sounds good. For the mid-point we want to see both raw numbers and a few sample summaries flagged for QA.
07:12 Jordan Lee: We'll include a sample set and a quality spreadsheet with annotator notes.
07:15 Raj Patel: Anything else about integration? We'll likely iterate on the API contract; is there a recommended pattern?
07:21 Maya Patel: We recommend a microservice pattern where you call Redwood's inference endpoint with a request ID and metadata; we support synchronous and streaming responses, plus function/tool-calling style outputs if you want structured data.
07:35 Tom Alvarez: Ok. Let's confirm milestones and dates. Kickoff today, access setup by 2026-09-21, baseline benchmarks complete by 2026-09-30, mid-point review week of 2026-10-05, extended runs by 2026-10-12, exec readout week of 2026-10-19.
07:56 Maya Patel: I'll put those in the SOW. Anything blocking on your side?
08:00 Leah Ortiz: We need to review the security pack before peering. Once that's approved we'll open the network.
08:06 Dr. Sarah Kim: We'll get the redacted dataset to you by 2026-09-17.
08:09 Maya Patel: Great. I'll send SOW and security docs by end of day tomorrow. Jordan will follow up on access steps.
08:15 Tom Alvarez: Thank you.
08:17 Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, I'll recap actions after the call.
08:20 (end)

Notes: transcript contains a few mis-transcribed product names and technical terms; timestamps approximate.
